meta.title: The True Cost of a Double-Digit Raise

scenes.narration: How to calculate the hidden traps of job switching and maximize your true wealth velocity

Picture this: you land a shiny 12% raise at a new job, and your brain immediately does a happy dance. But could that double-digit bump actually cost you money? Think of it like trading a dependable old car for a flashy sports car that constantly devours premium fuel—the initial thrill masks some serious hidden maintenance traps. Federal Reserve data shows job switchers outpace stayers in wage growth on paper, but walk away at the wrong time and you might regret it.

scenes.narration: Why would a higher paycheck backfire? Think of a three-year vesting cliff as a sheer mountain climb where your company stock ownership sits at zero percent until day one thousand ninety-five, when it spikes straight to one hundred percent. If you walk away just thirty days shy, you forfeit every single penny of unvested employer matching funds.

scenes.narration: You might be wondering: what about the psychological toll of changing teams? Beyond spreadsheets and vesting schedules, every career transition carries an emotional weight. The uncertainty of leaving familiar colleagues and the silent pressure of resetting your professional clock shape your journey far more than base salary alone.
